class.name: FellowWeathering3D
class.brief_description: Years of weather on a scene's buildings, from their shape: streaks under the ledges, damp at the walls' foot, a patina (FellowEngine).
class.description: Every opaque surface of the instances in [member cull_mask] is weathered as it is drawn (Forward+), with no textures and no painting. A patina varies the albedo's tone over metres ([member patina]). Streaks — dark lanes, each its own width, length and darkness — hang from the nearest ledge above a wall's point (a sill, a cornice, a balcony, an eave) and thin and fade down the wall over about [member streak_length] ([member streaks], [member stain_color]); there are none under a mass that rises on (a recessed window, a jetty), which shelters the wall. Damp darkens the foot of a wall up to a ragged tide line about [member damp_height] above the ground, with a broken band of salt above it and the splashes' grime in its lowest 35 cm ([member damp], [member damp_color]); the ground is the lower of what lies half a metre and a metre and a half out from the wall, so a balcony's floor over the street is not taken for it. The node finds the ledges and the ground in the scene's shape seen from above in horizontal layers: a stack of [member heightfield_layers] heightfields (particle collision heightfields of its own, seen by no particles), each [member heightfield_layer_height] tall, up from the node's height, [member heightfield_size] wide around the camera; each layer holds its highest surface, so that a sill is seen under the cornice above it. Place the node just under the lowest ground. The layers are drawn again when the camera has moved a sixteenth of [member heightfield_size], one a frame (or every frame, [member heightfield_always_update]); only the instances in [member cull_mask] are drawn into them — keep characters and other moving things out of it. Albedo only, multiplied (metallic surfaces less); every pattern fades to its mean where it is finer than a pixel. One node at a time is active: the last one to enter the tree. Without one, or hidden, nothing changes. [code]rendering/fellow/fluid/enabled[/code] off stops it. The Mobile and Compatibility renderers draw no weathering. Decision record [code]docs/decisions/0332-weathering.md[/code].

members.member: The render layers ([member VisualInstance3D.layers]) of the instances that are weathered and that form the ledges and the ground in the layers.
How strong the damp at the walls' foot is (0..1).
What full damp multiplies the albedo by.
How high the damp rises above the ground, in metres (its tide line varies from 0.7 to 1.3 times this along the wall).
If [code]true[/code], the layers are drawn again every frame (geometry that moves); otherwise when the camera has moved a sixteenth of [member heightfield_size] or a property changes.
Each layer's height, in metres. A layer sees one ledge over each point, its highest: about half a storey keeps a window's sill and the hood over it in different layers.
How many layers are stacked up from the node's height (1 to 16). Above the top one nothing is weathered but the patina.
Each layer's texels across [member heightfield_size] (256 to 8192). A ledge narrower than about two texels is missed. Each layer takes 4 bytes a texel of video memory.
The layers' width around the camera, in metres. Beyond it walls get the patina only.
How much the albedo's tone varies over metres (0..1).
Moves every pattern: the streaks' lanes, the tide line, the patina.
What a full streak multiplies the albedo by.
How far below a ledge the streaks fade, in metres (each lane 0.4 to 1.6 times this).
The whole weathering's strength (0..1); 0 draws none.
